ra: Hades is the ruler of the underworld, the House of Hades that bears his name (Homer, passim).
Persephone reigns as queen of the underworld alongside Hades (Homer Odyssey 10-11; Homeric Hymn to Demeter).
The underworld is ruled by Hades, its eponymous lord.
In the developed topography (Virgil Aeneid 6) Elysium is a region within the underworld.
The Asphodel Meadow is part of the House of Hades, where ordinary shades wander (Odyssey 11.539).
The Lugentes Campi are a named region of the underworld (Aeneid 6.441).
The Plain of Lethe lies within the underworld, where souls prepare for rebirth (Aeneid 6.703ff).
The Fields of Punishment are the penal region of the underworld (Aeneid 6.548ff).
The Fields of Punishment lie above and continuous with the abyss of Tartarus, where the deepest torments occur (Aeneid 6; Hesiod Theogony 717ff).
The Fields of Punishment are encircled by the flaming river Phlegethon (Aeneid 6.550-551).
The Plain of Lethe takes its name from and is watered by the river Lethe of forgetfulness (Aeneid 6.705, 714).
Erebus, primordial darkness, is the gloom of the underworld through which the dead pass (Hesiod Theogony 123; Homer).
In Hesiod's account (and Pindar Ol. 2), Cronus rules over the Isles of the Blest where the heroic dead dwell apart from Hades' realm.
Rhadamanthus presides over the punishment of the wicked in the penal region (Aeneid 6.566-569).
The Isles of the Blest and Elysium are the two principal Greek paradise-abodes, frequently conflated in later sources as the destination of the blessed.
